extra.message: Reflected XSS: the GET parameter 'name' is read at app/blueprints/sandboxes/views.py:13 (request.args.get('name', 'world!')) and rendered with the '| safe' Jinja filter, which disables auto-escaping. Requesting /sandbox/unsafe_params?name=<script>alert(1)</script> executes arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's browser.

Unsanitized user input from request.args.get('name') is passed directly to render_template('sandboxes/unsafe_params.html') at line 14, where it is rendered with the '| safe' filter (unsafe_params.html:6). This is the taint source for a reflected XSS vulnerability.

Cookie-based XSS: the 'name' value comes from request.cookies.get('name') / request.form.get('name') (app/blueprints/sandboxes/views.py:27-28) and is rendered with the '| safe' filter, disabling escaping. An attacker who can set the cookie or POST the form value can execute arbitrary JavaScript when the page is viewed.

User-controlled input (request.form.get('name')) and the existing cookie (line 27) are stored via response.set_cookie (line 38) and rendered unescaped with '| safe' in unsafe_cookies.html:6, enabling cookie-based XSS. This is the taint source.

Stored XSS: message content is rendered with the '| safe' filter, disabling auto-escaping. The value is attacker-controlled via the unauthenticated API MessagesView.post (app/blueprints/api/views.py:43-56) and via the feedback form (app/blueprints/account_area/views.py:66-77), so arbitrary JavaScript executes in the admin's browser when messages are viewed.

Stored XSS: message.from_user is rendered with the '| safe' filter. The API MessagesView.post accepts an arbitrary 'from_user' value from request JSON without validation (app/blueprints/api/views.py:50), allowing an attacker to inject HTML/JavaScript that executes in the admin panel.

MessagesView.post has no authentication decorator (unlike index/get/delete which use @admin_required). Any unauthenticated client can POST JSON to the message API and store arbitrary message/from_user content that is later rendered with the '| safe' filter in the admin panel, enabling unauthenticated stored XSS and message injection.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: Stored XSS: g.user.username is rendered with the '| safe' filter in the global navigation bar, which is included on every page. If a username containing HTML/JavaScript is stored in the User table, the payload executes in the browser of every user viewing the page. Usernames are not escaped anywhere before this sink.

Open redirect: the 'next' query parameter is read at line 11 (request.args.get('next', url_for('index'))) and passed directly to redirect() with no allowlist or validation. An attacker can craft /toggle_xss_protection/?next=https://evil.example to redirect users to an arbitrary external site for phishing.

Passwords are stored in plaintext in a String(200) column with no hashing. Login compares plaintext directly (app/blueprints/login/views.py:17: user.password == password), and password changes write plaintext (app/blueprints/account_area/views.py:34-36). Anyone with database or backup access obtains all user passwords in cleartext.

cwe: CWE-256: Plaintext Storage of a Password

extra.message: User.serialize includes the plaintext password ('password': self.password). This serialization is used by the Users API (app/blueprints/api/views.py:72), so any code path returning user.serialize exposes all users' plaintext passwords. Passwords should never be included in serialized representations.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: The Flask SECRET_KEY is hardcoded as the literal string 'Keep it secret, keep it safe'. This key signs session cookies and Flask-Login state; anyone with source access can forge valid session cookies for any user (including admin), bypassing authentication entirely.

The add_admin management command defaults the admin password to the hardcoded value 'admin'. Running the documented setup (python manage.py add_admin) creates an admin account with a publicly known password, allowing trivial privileged access.

The login page displays the admin credentials 'admin/admin' in plain text to every visitor. Combined with the default password in manage.py:14, this discloses working administrator credentials and enables direct privilege escalation.

Flask debug mode is enabled (app.config['DEBUG'] = True) and the app is started with app.run() at line 96. This activates the Werkzeug interactive debugger, exposing stack traces, source snippets and local variables on exceptions, and potentially allowing remote code execution if the debugger console is reachable.

The after_request handler explicitly sets the X-XSS-Protection response header to 0 whenever session['xss_protection_enabled'] is false (the default), disabling the browser's reflective XSS filter on every response and weakening defense in depth against the application's XSS flaws.

response.set_cookie('name', name) sets a user-controlled cookie without HttpOnly, Secure, or SameSite attributes. The lack of HttpOnly exposes the value to JavaScript (amplifying the cookie XSS in unsafe_cookies.html:6), the lack of Secure allows transmission over plaintext HTTP, and the lack of SameSite broadens CSRF exposure.

The change_password POST endpoint is protected only by @login_required and validates no CSRF token. The rendered form (components/forms.html) contains no csrf_token field. An attacker can auto-submit a cross-origin form to change the victim's password (lines 34-37), resulting in account takeover.

The change_email POST endpoint is protected only by @login_required and validates no CSRF token. An attacker can forge a cross-origin request that changes the authenticated victim's email address (lines 54-56), compromising account recovery and identity.
